title: Multivalent supramolecular fluorescent probes for accurate disease imaging

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, second paragraph (Current strategies for mitigating MPS capture...)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states that conjugating hydrophilic moieties such as polyethylene glycol (PEG) 'increases the renal clearance rate' and 'concurrently shortens circulation half-life.' This is factually misleading for PEG: PEGylation is commonly used to reduce renal clearance and prolong circulation half-life, not to increase renal clearance. The blanket statement therefore misrepresents standard imaging-probe design and likely overgeneralizes the cited literature.
